translation_notes: prefixes: RDFS->rdfs, RDF->rdf, XSD->xsd, SKOS->skos, SH->sh

This is the trap the previous trav_navigation batch flagged: propShape is a real subject shared by sh:path/sh:name/sh:description/sh:defaultValue, but each read is independently-optional and the original relies on a bare `for` loop leaving its variable untouched (last value, or the previous propShape's leftover) when the predicate is absent. Fusing the four into one conjunctive m{ } would silently drop any propShape missing one predicate (defaultValue is optional in the fixture) instead of reproducing that leftover-value quirk, so each stayed a separate trav_one_step m{ }
(s, RDF.type, SH.NodeShape) in shape became bool(m{ {s} rdf:type sh:NodeShape }(shape)) (trav_existence), not a graph-membership Python idiom

the outer shape.triples((None, SKOS.example, None)) unpacked (s, p, o) but never used p (always SKOS.example, a fixed predicate); translated as m{ ?s skos:example ?o } and dropped the unused binding rather than inventing a variable for a predicate that is not data-dependent

shapeProc mutates module-level nodeLabels/nodeLink and returns None, with dataGraph only read: entry=/fixture= would see nothing, so driver.py instead has both sides call shapeProc against fixture.ttl (dataGraph) and a second file shape.ttl (the shape graph shapeProc parses itself from a path) and print the resulting dicts for module-state stdout comparison

shape.namespace_manager is untouched by the ldpy @prefix declarations (those bind lexical prefixes for the island source, not the parsed shape graph's namespace manager), so .n3() output is identical on both sides

repair.driver: shape.ttl gains the repository's own shape form (ex:PlaceShape: anonymous property shapes, a sh:defaultValue labelled in dataGraph, an empty sh:description), two non-NodeShapes that have skos:example AND a sh:property (typed sh:PropertyShape; rdfs:seeAlso sh:NodeShape), and one neighbour per bound predicate (rdfs:seeAlso, sh:targetClass, rdfs:comment); fixture.ttl gains the default value's label and a skos:note beside it. The single call in the artefacts' driving code is unchanged.

optimization_notes: optimized.py: the shape graph is parsed in one statement (`Graph().parse(..., format=util.guess_format(...))`); `shape.namespace_manager`, used six times, gets a local name (ns_manager); `shape.triples((None, SKOS.example, None))` with an unused p becomes `subject_objects`; inst is built in one statement (the brackets hold no < or >); the defaultValue loop iterates as nodeValURL (the copy goes) and uses `+=`; `str()` of strings goes; the nodeLabels if/else loses its `not`. Every leftover-value quirk of the bare loops is kept (path, nodeLb, nodeURL keep the previous property shape's value when a predicate is missing, and path or nodeURL still raise UnboundLocalError when the first one has none). The if/else is not turned into `setdefault(inst, {})[path] = ...`: with path unbound, setdefault would leave an empty dict in the module-level nodeLabels before raising.

optimized.ldpy, from optimized.py: `@graph shape` (checked: on a Graph() it adds no namespace binding, and it never overwrites one, so n3() output is unchanged) makes the six shape reads receiver-less islands: `m{ ?s skos:example ?o }`, the existence guard `m{ {s} a sh:NodeShape }` (bool() goes: it is an if test), and the five single-step `m{ {propShape} sh:P ?v }` reads; each is one to three tokens shorter than the call it replaces (measured). The dataGraph read stays `dataGraph.objects(nodeValURL, rdfs:label)` by rule 4: as `m{ ... }(dataGraph)` it is one token longer.
No exception to the symmetry. The four property-shape reads are not fused: each is optional and relies on the bare loop's leftover value.
header_optimization_notes: Python: URIRef, Namespace, NamespaceManager and XSD go (json, Path and Graph stay for the driving code); the rdflib.namespace names are sorted.
LD Python: URIRef and Namespace go; @prefix rdf: (the guard writes `a`) and xsd: (only inside a string) go.
